title: The googol
hook: A nine-year-old named the number 1 followed by a hundred zeros.
peek: A googol is 1 followed by 100 zeros, more than the number of atoms in the observable universe. Its name came from a nine-year-old boy asked by his mathematician uncle, and a misspelling of it later named a search engine.
lede: Around 1920 the American mathematician Edward Kasner wanted a friendly name for a very large number, 1 followed by 100 zeros. He asked his nine-year-old nephew, Milton Sirotta, what to call it. Milton suggested googol. Kasner liked it enough to put it in print, and a child's made-up word became a recognised mathematical term.

bullets.text: Kasner made the word famous in Mathematics and the Imagination, a 1940 popular book written with James Newman. He used the googol to show that a number can be huge yet still exactly defined.
A googol is far larger than the number of atoms in the observable universe, usually estimated at around 10 to the power 80. Yet it is easy to write down: 10 to the power 100.

Milton also proposed the googolplex, which he described as a 1 followed by zeros until your hand gets tired. Kasner fixed it as 1 followed by a googol zeros, a number with too many digits to write out in the universe.
The search engine's name is the googol misspelt. The usual story is that the spelling google came from a slip while checking whether a web address was free.
